question.prompt: Jack and Jill run \(10\) kilometers. They start at the same point, run \(5\) kilometers up a hill, and return to the starting point by the same route. Jack has a \(10\)-minute head start and runs at the rate of \(15\) km/hr uphill and \(20\) km/hr downhill. Jill runs \(16\) km/hr uphill and \(22\) km/hr downhill. How far from the top of the hill are they when they pass going in opposite directions?

solutions.explanation:
Consider the instant Jack reaches the top, because this is when they begin running toward each other. His uphill trip takes
\[
\frac{5}{15}=\frac13\text{ hour}=20\text{ minutes}.
\]
Jill started \(10\) minutes later, so she has then run for \(10\) minutes, or \(1/6\) hour. She has covered \(16\cdot\frac16=\frac83\) km and is
\[
5-\frac83=\frac73\text{ km}
\]
below the top.

Jack now runs downhill at \(20\) km/hr while Jill runs uphill at \(16\) km/hr. Together they close the gap at \(20+16=36\) km/hr, so they meet after
\[
\frac{7/3}{36}=\frac7{108}\text{ hour}.
\]
During this time Jack descends
\[
20\cdot\frac7{108}=\frac{35}{27}\text{ km}.
\]
This is less than \(5\) km, and Jill covers only \(16\cdot\frac7{108}=\frac{28}{27}<\frac73\) km, so both are still on the claimed parts of their trips. The gap decreases at a constant positive rate, giving exactly one meeting while they run in opposite directions. Their distance from the top is \(\boxed{\frac{35}{27}\text{ km}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Start when Jack reaches the top

solutions.explanation:
Jack reaches the top \(5/15=1/3\) hour after he starts. Jill starts \(1/6\) hour later and needs \(5/16\) hour to climb, so Jack reaches the top first.

Let \(d\) be their distance in kilometers below the top when Jack is descending and Jill is ascending, with \(0<d<5\). Jack has run \(5\) km uphill and \(d\) km downhill, while Jill has run \(5-d\) km uphill. Jack's elapsed running time must be \(1/6\) hour longer than Jill's:
\[
\frac5{15}+\frac d{20}
=\frac16+\frac{5-d}{16}.
\]
Multiplying every term by \(240\) gives
\[
80+12d=40+75-15d.
\]
Hence \(27d=35\), so \(d=35/27\). This lies strictly between \(0\) and \(5\), confirming that Jack is still descending and Jill is still ascending. The equation has a unique solution, so the requested distance is \(\boxed{\frac{35}{27}\text{ km}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Compare their elapsed running times
